what: Procurement has two views instead of four (Needs & catalogue, Contracts) and fewer controls. The suggestion now judges 'late' on every delivery option. When standard delivery is late but priority is on time, it suggests that offer with priority preselected. When nothing is on time, it suggests the earliest arrival instead of the cheapest and slowest one. The suggested offer carries a plain 'Suggested' chip. Its footer says what it is: 'Suggested: on time[ only with priority delivery], within budget, then the lightest fitting part from its most reliable supplier', or 'No offer arrives on time: suggested is the earliest arrival'. Every offer row shows the date and price of the option it would be ordered with, which is the option preselected when it is picked. The decision at signing (price, arrival, Science-test window, reliability, budget left) sits in the order dialog and the inspector footer: 'Cheapest on time: …', 'More reliable on time: …', and 'Shared budget after: X M free · ≈ Y M spare once all parts are bought'. The header keeps its single budget figure (Available budget with Committed / Spent / Funding). The per-station split is not shown anywhere: `spendByStation` and `stillToBuy` are exported from rules.ts for a later cross-station step. Calls for Offers is gone as a tab. A need that is beyond research shows its two routes with dates, prices and reliability ('Wait for Science …' vs 'Tender now …'), and a Call is opened from there. Partner and tender offers appear in the need's own offer list, with a chip on the need row. Before the Planner orders, the Planner's draft parts are listed as read-only 'Draft' needs with Order-by dates, offers and the suggested price. After everything is contracted, every timeline row says 'time to test' or 'no time to test', with margins in whole days. A late or untestable contract offers one 'Speed up · priority' action. A contract on its way can be switched to another offer in one all-or-nothing step: the new order is checked on the post-cancellation state before anything is cancelled. Procurement's UI state resets on a new attempt.

It needs a case where the new order is rejected after cancelling, which I could not produce by clicking, and no switch was confirmed in any session. Whole-day margins after a Comms delivery slip: the rounding is in the code, but no slip happened in the repair session. onGameReset: this checkout has no restart button (package A). risk: The switch is a new lever: it trades the cancellation loss (30-70 % at signing, rising to 100 %) for reliability or speed. It is priced by the existing refund rule and only works on contracts still on their way, but it gives spare budget a use. With 200+ M unspent it may make reliability cheap to buy; balance is unchecked. Priority delivery, also as a speed-up, is cheap (0.1-0.7 M fees seen), so 'time to test' is easy to reach for parts with a priority option. That makes Science's part tests more available than edf688e assumed. Flexible delivery is hidden, not deleted (data and reducers still accept it). The mass-first ranking from edf688e is kept: on Mars the order dialog showed a heavier part that was both cheaper and more reliable than the suggestion, and the dialog names it. 'Still to buy' (Procurement, suggested offers) and the Planner's '≈ N M to buy' (planner estimate) differ: on Mars 243 M against 195 M. Removed reducers: openRequestCall, allocateDepartment, release, closeCall. An old save with department allocations still loads and they still count, but they can no longer be created or released. The cancel token no longer includes the refund: the refund shown is live and the reducer books the refund of the floored game day. A player who confirms on a day boundary gets about 0.1 M less than displayed. usePView now floors the calendar day (fewer re-renders); arrivals are whole days as before.
foreignRequests: Cross-station budget step (A/B for the Planner, D2 for Comms, Science unowned): put one shared figure on all four stations. Procurement exports two pure functions from stations/procurement/rules.ts, both unused by the Procurement header for now. `spendByStation(state, scienceInfo)` splits spending into parts / science / comms from each station's own records. `stillToBuy(view)` gives the suggested price of every need not yet contracted, drafts included. The Planner's TopBar chip (`toBuy = ev.uncontractedCostM`) currently disagrees with Procurement's 'Still to buy' (Mars: 195 M against 243 M).
